{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-hi-x","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"bcd2a9fca500f7e7c2c29c8d8f3c80be73f50363fb9ba61684e238aa14865e90","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-hi-class-3:lineage:98","source_registry_sha256":"1323c0f691f132d6e9e9a263c68306b972b82c8bbaa5a48a33a79177660764be","source_liveness_sha256":"27cf6d56fae2d5323c61bcbb69f0d992aeceb71a7dae4302b1f14baa17651cb0"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C2"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C2","chunk_id":"C2.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Traffic Laws and Regulations","heading":"C2 — KG hints for Traffic Laws and Regulations","learner_facing":false,"markdown":"## C2 — KG hints for Traffic Laws and Regulations

FACT_ID: sec06-R01 | anchor: A02
A turn or lane-change signal must begin at least one hundred feet ahead, while a railroad stop must be at least fifteen feet from the nearest rail [A02].
Why it matters: group_hint distances; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint two; confusable_with sec06-F10 and sec06-F13.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec06-R02 | anchor: A05
Passing is banned within one hundred feet of an intersection, railroad crossing, narrow bridge, viaduct or tunnel [A06], while a hill or curve requires seven hundred to one thousand feet of clear distance before passing [A05].
Why it matters: group_hint no-passing; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint two; confusable_with sec06-F34 and sec06-F31.
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec06-R03 | anchor: A03
Parking must be within twelve inches of the curb, while a street must keep at least ten feet of width free for traffic beside a parked vehicle [A03].
Why it matters: group_hint parking; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint two; confusable_with sec06-F20 and sec06-F21.
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec06-R04 | anchor: A07
When vehicles approach an intersection at the same time, yield to the car on the right, while a driver turning left must yield to oncoming traffic that is close enough to pose a hazard [A07].
Why it matters: group_hint right-of-way; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint two; confusable_with sec06-F35 and sec06-F37.
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec06-R05 | anchor: A07
Entering from an alley, driveway or farmyard requires a full stop and yield, while entering a protected route from a side road requires yielding to the protected traffic [A07].
Why it matters: group_hint right-of-way; prereq_hint sec06-R04; difficulty_hint two; confusable_with sec06-F36 and sec06-F35.
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec06-R06 | anchor: A01
You may use the left half of a two or three lane road to pass when no traffic is coming, while on a road with four or more lanes the left half is off limits unless signs direct otherwise [A01].
Why it matters: group_hint keeping-right; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint two; confusable_with sec06-F03 and sec06-F04.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec06-R07 | anchor: A05
Passing on the right is allowed when the vehicle ahead is turning left or when two or more lanes run your way [A01], while passing on the right shoulder is never allowed [A05].
Why it matters: group_hint passing; prereq_hint sec06-R06; difficulty_hint two; confusable_with sec06-F05 and sec06-F31.
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec06-R08 | anchor: A04
For an approaching emergency vehicle you pull out of its path and stop, while for a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights you slow or stop and leave an empty lane beside it when safe [A04].
Why it matters: group_hint emergency-vehicles; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint two; confusable_with sec06-F27 and sec06-F28.
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec06-R09 | anchor: A03
Driving below a posted minimum limit is a violation, while driving so slowly that you hold back traffic is a violation even where no minimum is posted [A03].
Why it matters: group_hint speed; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint two; confusable_with sec06-F15 and sec06-F16.
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec06-R10 | anchor: A04
A vehicle may stay parked on a public street for up to twenty-four hours continuously, while in a tow-away zone even a momentary stop during the posted hours is prohibited [A04].
Why it matters: group_hint parking; prereq_hint sec06-R03; difficulty_hint one; confusable_with sec06-F22 and sec06-F24.
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec06-R11 | anchor: A06
The slow-moving vehicle emblem is an eighteen-inch reflective triangle for vehicles built for twenty-five miles per hour or less [A05], while the no passing zone pennant is a yellow sign on the left side of the road [A06].
Why it matters: group_hint signs-in-law; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint one; confusable_with sec06-F30 and sec06-F33.
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec06-R12 | anchor: A04
Funeral processions and convoys hold the right of way at intersections, while emergency vehicles take the right of way everywhere by requiring you to clear a path and stop [A04].
Why it matters: group_hint right-of-way; prereq_hint sec06-R08; difficulty_hint one; confusable_with sec06-F29 and sec06-F27.
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec06-R13 | anchor: A02
Hand signals replace turn signals only when the vehicle's signals are not working, while resting a foot on the brake pedal creates a false stop signal and must be avoided [A02].
Why it matters: group_hint signals; prereq_hint sec06-R01; difficulty_hint one; confusable_with sec06-F11 and sec06-F12.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0027]
